question: What is the primary goal of disinfection in a clinical setting?

options.A: Reducing pathogens on inanimate surfaces to safe levels
options.D: Enhancing the shine of surgical instruments

explanation: Disinfection specifically lowers pathogen counts on non-living objects to prevent transmission, whereas destroying spores requires full sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why does disinfection differ fundamentally from sterilization?

options.A: Sterilization targets inanimate objects while disinfection targets skin
options.B: Sterilization uses chemical liquids instead of physical heat
options.C: Disinfection kills bacterial spores while sterilization does not
options.D: Disinfection reduces pathogens but may not eliminate all spores

explanation: Sterilization achieves total elimination of all microbial life including hard spores, whereas standard disinfection does not guarantee spore destruction. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which process must always happen before disinfection can be effective?
explanation: Organic matter like blood or feces protects underlying microorganisms and deactivates disinfectants, making thorough cleaning an essential prerequisite. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h2)

question: A nurse wipes down a treatment trolley with a chemical solution that kills most bacteria and viruses, but leaves bacterial spores intact. What process has occurred?
explanation: Killing vegetative pathogens while leaving spores behind defines the level of action characteristic of disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h2)

question: High-level disinfection is required for which category of patient care items?

options.A: Critical items entering sterile body cavities

explanation: Semi-critical equipment like endoscopy scopes touch mucous membranes and demand high-level disinfection to prevent infection transmission. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing a stethoscope that touched only the intact chest skin of a patient. What level of disinfection is sufficient?
explanation: Items contacting only intact skin are classified as non-critical and require only low-level disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the standard concentration of alcohol commonly used as an effective skin and surface disinfectant?
explanation: A 70 percent aqueous solution of alcohol provides optimal water content to facilitate protein coagulation and cellular penetration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why are glutaraldehyde and ortho-phthalaldehyde frequently chosen for flexible endoscopes?

options.A: They achieve high-level disinfection without damaging heat-sensitive instruments
options.B: They eliminate the need for prior mechanical washing of the device
options.C: They leave a protective residual film that prevents future bacterial growth
options.D: They neutralize bacterial spores instantly within two minutes of exposure

explanation: Aldehydes offer high-level disinfection suitable for delicate, heat-sensitive medical devices like endoscopes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why does wiping away a heavy blood spill before applying disinfectant matter so much?

options.A: Protein layers attract more airborne fungi to the surface
options.B: Dried blood speeds up the evaporation of liquid chemicals
options.C: Blood makes the metal instrument slippery to hold
options.D: Organic matter binds and neutralizes chemical disinfectant potency

explanation: Blood and other organic soils create a physical barrier and chemically react with disinfectants, lowering their active concentration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h5)

question: What critical parameter specified by the manufacturer must a nurse strictly observe during chemical disinfection?
explanation: Disinfectants require a specific duration of wet contact with the surface to successfully destroy targeted pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h5)

question: How should a nurse wipe a treatment table to prevent spreading contamination?

options.B: In circular motions covering the entire table at once
options.C: From clean areas moving outward to dirty areas
options.D: From the dirtiest areas toward the cleanest areas

explanation: Wiping from clean to dirty prevents dragging heavy microbial loads back across freshly sanitized surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why must chlorine disinfectant solutions be freshly prepared on a daily basis?

options.A: Microorganisms grow inside closed chlorine containers overnight
options.B: Active chlorine evaporates and loses potency over time
options.C: Fresh solutions change color to indicate readiness
options.D: Standard hospital policy forbids reusing plastic buckets

explanation: Chlorine solutions degrade rapidly when exposed to air and light, rendering older dilutions ineffective against pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which personal protective equipment is essential when diluting concentrated liquid disinfectants?

options.B: Paper face mask and examination gloves
options.C: Sterile surgical cap and shoe covers

explanation: Concentrated chemicals pose a severe splash hazard to the eyes and skin, requiring protective eyewear and robust gloves. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary reason for ensuring good ventilation in hospital utility rooms where disinfectants are mixed?

options.A: Lowering the room temperature for staff comfort
options.B: Reducing the humidity that attracts dust mites
options.C: Accelerating the drying time of washed instruments
options.D: Preventing the buildup of toxic chemical vapors

explanation: Inhaling concentrated fumes from active chemicals like chlorine or aldehydes can cause respiratory irritation and chronic lung issues. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h7)
